shortlist.title: Document direction separates a label reference from a repeated caption
shortlist.consequence: A fixed backward-reference constructor must obtain its particular owner from an earlier written/labelled record; a forward-introduced repeated caption need not. For complete owned bridges, reversing the available antecedent order changes whether that fixed reference construction can bind.
shortlist.native_owner_use: Singular inscription ownership establishes the candidate endpoint. It does not identify which prose occurrence refers to it.
shortlist.frequency_composition_use: Require all exact whole occurrences, directions, dispersion and entry contexts to fit the same paid reference/name account; frequency supplies exposure/countercases, not reference semantics. Keep ordered parts, exact whole residual and context-conditioned wrappers separately.
shortlist.decisive_failure: An independently coded reference occurs where the fixed backward contract has no admissible earlier owner, or it picks the wrong owner; unread possible antecedents make result UNKNOWN.
missing_inputs: Exact current label readings and alternate-reader whole boundaries are root-owned and not read here.
One complete prose unit plus a legitimate written reference/owner binding, not merely exact repetition.
Independent role coding and fixed document order; local direction alone cannot distinguish name from reference.
known_predecessors: GDT790 nine usable multi-character exact edges are occurrence links, not translated references.
GDT890 cannot establish complete component/port topology or ownership; repeated opener does not repair that missing data.
GDT798 retains reference/remedy C0 tie and opaque null; running-only/profile purity is insufficient.
shortlist.novelty: Existing card retained; not a new direction experiment. New singular current owner could improve one endpoint, but no complete semantic endpoint asserted.
shortlist.feasibility: Only potentially useful after root supplies complete current binding and an actual unequal direction/role duty. No held confirmation or portable grammar from the three labels.

shortlist.title: Caption and prose channels select different argument arity on one diagram page
shortlist.consequence: A fixed caption construction can denote one independently owned component/part; a prose use of the same whole may fill a written argument slot rather than a standalone assertion. A channel-conditioned contract must specify which slots are licensed and bind them without implicit patients. A competing single shared grammar must account for the same units.
shortlist.native_owner_use: Root-owned native inscription-to-fragment binding establishes caption channel/unit. It does not give its lexical type or argument arity.
shortlist.frequency_composition_use: Whole-word profile must account for any prose uses under the frozen slot rule; same whole can be a caption and an argument without different meanings. Known composition forbids freely replacing a family by unrelated macros; whole residual and entry context remain paid.
shortlist.decisive_failure: The exact frozen channel contract cannot bind its owed arguments at a complete unit boundary, or supposedly different channels have the same independently established argument duty. Unknown scope prevents an arity decision.
missing_inputs: Complete native label unit, not assumed one word before root glyph binding.
A complete corresponding prose construction with actual written participants and scope.
An independent argument/type duty: word count or short label length is not arity.
known_predecessors: GDT213 supports mixed component-caption/prose document architecture, not Voynich semantic roles;22/23 oldq13 owners proximity-only.
IDEA57 curation repairs only quotation/source span; reconsider reports NO_REVIEWED_REOPENING_CONTRACT, no science approval.
GDT810 rejects one-value-per-hypothesized-quality inference; multiple repeated values do not independently determine semantic arity.
shortlist.novelty: Existing method-unreviewed card retained. Current singular owner is a possible changed endpoint, not a fulfilled channel/arity gate.
shortlist.feasibility: A finite C0 complete construction is allowed if roles and different consequence are fixed; no need confirmed words. With only a label-owner and frequencies this remains unready.

shortlist.title: A closure token marks an exhaustive list rather than another list item
shortlist.consequence: A fixed exhaustivity operator commits to every member of its written bounded category; an ordinary final caption merely names another member. One independently known omitted member rejects the closed-list contract even when all surviving named items are correctly owned.
shortlist.native_owner_use: A complete native row can delimit pictured owners and label assignments. It does not establish the exhaustive semantic category, whether every picture is a list member, or whether the last inscription is closure.
shortlist.frequency_composition_use: A prospective closure form must have all exact uses accounted for at licensed boundaries; terminal dispersion alone gives no ALL or END meaning. Shared formal endings cannot be erased or assigned universal closure semantics.
shortlist.decisive_failure: A complete closure-bearing record omits an independently owned member of that same bounded category, or the frozen closure construction occurs in an independently open list.
missing_inputs: An independently defined finite category and membership/end boundary, not the number of current labels.
A complete written list with a genuine exhaustivity duty and exact closure candidate.
A countercase capable of distinguishing omitted versus outside-scope members.
known_predecessors: GDT942 finds no visible list-total binding; ordinary spaces/three forms do not select a numeral or a list.
GA426 EACH convention does not entail repeated surface quantities; compact scope remains live.
shortlist.novelty: Existing raw mechanism retained; no repeated count/kerning route and no new raw card.
shortlist.feasibility: Lower readiness. Three owned labels alone cannot fulfill the membership/exhaustivity prerequisite; no test recommended from the current root task alone.

shortlist.title: A following value token denotes a domain-specific measurement, not a universal ordinal
shortlist.consequence: Within a fully owned fixed value construction, a common written value may require different unit/reference-basis interpretation under different field heads. A later equality/order comparison is licensed only on compatible axes or an explicit conversion. An unchanged numerical ordinal can still operate across different domains, so domain difference alone is not a falsifier.
shortlist.native_owner_use: A singular pictured owner may bind the measured/graded entity; it does not give the value axis, number, unit or measured property.
shortlist.frequency_composition_use: Exact label/prose whole recurrence and field-head/value profiles constrain complete usage. No amount or rank value follows from aN/final strokes, high frequency or a repeated X-value adjacency.
shortlist.decisive_failure: An exact frozen unit/basis contract predicts a later incompatible comparison without written conversion, or misses an independently specified scope/scale consequence. If ordinal3 and calibrated3 make the same prediction, retain tie.
missing_inputs: A complete owned written head/value construction, not just a graphical caption.
An independently constrained axis or conversion/comparison duty distinguishing both exact contracts.
All scopes, patients and existing word priors retained; no free new field values chosen to create a mismatch.
known_predecessors: GDT764 five triple fields and nine exact pairs provide working record architecture; axes and III are unconfirmed assumptions.
GA849 and raw49 are close relatives; parked W94–96 f2v identity/unit repairs remain closed.
Native owner alone cannot turn a nominal field into a measurement.
shortlist.novelty: Existing raw narrower domain-value rival retained, not a new numeral route. Raw definition still has historical draft_not_added wording while currentregistry is imported-unreviewed.
shortlist.feasibility: Lowest present readiness: the original domain-switch contrast permits a portable ordinal too. Needs a real different basis/comparison consequence before selection.
